overview.heading: What the dashboard shows
overview.body: The dashboard is the first page you see after signing in. It gives a quick snapshot of the whole warehouse: how many cells are empty, full, or opened; how many pallets are expired or expiring soon; and how much activity (pallets stored, opened, emptied, or transferred) happened today and this week.

productFilter.heading: Filtering by product
productFilter.body: Use the product selector at the top to narrow every tile on the dashboard down to one or more specific products — useful for checking how much stock of a particular item is on hand or about to expire.

grid.heading: What is a row?
grid.body: A row is one physical rack of storage in the warehouse, identified by a single letter (A, B, C…). Inside a row, storage space is arranged as a grid: a number of cells across, stacked on a number of levels.

dimensions.heading: Cells and levels
dimensions.body: A row's "Cells" number is how many storage positions sit side by side on one level, and "Levels" is how many of those levels are stacked on top of each other. Multiply them together and that's the total number of pallet slots the row holds — a row with 10 cells and 3 levels holds 30 pallets.

creating.heading: Adding a new row
creating.body: From the Rows page, click "Add row" and enter a letter plus the number of cells and levels. The system creates every empty slot in the grid automatically — there's nothing else to set up before pallets can be stored in it.

editing.heading: Changing a row's size
editing.body: Open a row and choose Edit to change its letter or its cells/levels count. The size can only be changed while the row is completely empty — if any slot in it currently holds a pallet, resizing is blocked until that pallet is moved or removed.

deleting.heading: Deleting a row
deleting.body: A row can be deleted from the Rows list, but only while it holds no pallets. If it still has stock in it, move or empty every slot first — the delete option is hidden and a "Has pallets" notice appears instead.

map.heading: Reading the map
map.body: The Cells page shows every row as a grid of storage cells, colored by what's inside them. Switch between the flat 2D view and the walkable 3D view, and use the search box to jump straight to a cell by its position (for example A12·3).

legend.heading: Cell colors
legend.body: These are the same colors and icons used throughout the app, including the activity log — so a cell's color always means the same thing wherever you see it.

managingPallets.heading: Storing, opening, and moving pallets
managingPallets.body: Click a cell to manage what's in it: store a new pallet in an empty cell, open a full pallet to start taking boxes out, remove more boxes from an already-open pallet, empty a pallet completely, or transfer it to a different cell. Every change is recorded in the activity log automatically.

deactivating.heading: Deactivating a cell
deactivating.body: If a cell becomes unusable — damaged shelving, for example — deactivate it so it can no longer be used to store, open, or move pallets, until you reactivate it again.

accounts.heading: Creating an account
accounts.body: From the Users page, click "Add user" and fill in a name, email, and password. Tick "Admin access" if the new account should be able to use this admin panel — leave it unticked for a warehouse worker who will only use the mobile scanning app.

roles.heading: What the roles mean
roles.body: There are two kinds of account. An Admin account can sign in here to manage rows, products, users, and view the full activity log. A Mobile user account can only use the phone/scanner app on the warehouse floor to store, open, and move pallets — it cannot sign in to this admin panel.

defaultBoxes.heading: Why every product starts at 50 boxes
defaultBoxes.body: Products themselves come from the main store system, not from this app, so this app doesn't know how many boxes actually fit on one pallet of a given product. Until someone sets the real number, every product is assumed to hold 50 boxes per full pallet so the rest of the system has something to work with.

settingBoxes.heading: Setting the real box count
settingBoxes.body: Go to the Products page, find the product, and edit the number in its "Boxes / pallet" column. Save it once and every full pallet of that product will use the real count from then on — you only need to do this the first time a product's true pallet size is known.

exportingQr.heading: Printing a product's QR label
exportingQr.body: Click the QR icon at the end of a product's row to download a printable QR label for it. One label represents the whole product, not a single pallet — print it once and stick a copy on every box/pallet of that product. Scanning the label in the mobile app looks up the product by its current name and picture, so a label printed today still works correctly even if the product's name changes later.

filtering.heading: Filtering the activity log
filtering.body: Open the Filters panel to narrow the list by product, pallet, row, column, the person who made the change, the type of action, or a date range. Combine as many filters as you need — for example, one product plus one row shows only that product's activity in that row.

actions.heading: What each action means
actions.stored: Stored — a pallet was placed into an empty cell.
actions.opened: Opened — someone started taking individual boxes out of a full pallet, without emptying it.
actions.boxesRemoved: Boxes removed — more boxes were taken from a pallet that was already open.
actions.emptied: Emptied — the last boxes were taken and the cell is now empty again.
actions.transferred: Transferred — a pallet was moved from one cell to another; the log shows both where it left and where it landed.
actions.deactivated: Deactivated — a cell was marked unusable (for example, damaged shelving) and can't hold pallets until it's reactivated.
actions.reactivated: Reactivated — a previously deactivated cell was marked usable again.

legend.heading: Cell colors
legend.body: These are the same colors and icons used on the Cells map, so what you see there matches what you see in the log.

what.heading: What is a verification round?
what.body: A verification round is a physical stock check: a warehouse worker walks the rows with the mobile app and confirms what's actually stored in each cell matches what the system expects. Each round is made up of individual reports, one per cell checked.

reports.heading: Correct and incorrect reports
reports.body: Open a round to see every report in it. Each one is marked correct when what the worker found matches the system, or incorrect when it doesn't — for example an empty cell that's actually holding a pallet, or the wrong product in a slot. Use this list to spot and fix real-world discrepancies.

exporting.heading: Exporting a round's reports
exporting.body: From a round's page, export its reports to a CSV file — useful for sharing results with someone who doesn't use this admin panel, or keeping an offline record.
